title: Indeterminate form
text: Substitute $$x$$ with the value $$x$$ approaches to. If the function results in one of these indeterminate form: $$\frac{0}{0}$$, $$\frac{\infty}{\infty}$$ or $$\frac{-\infty}{\infty}$$, we apply L’Hôpital’s Rule.

title: Apply L’Hôpital’s Rule
text: Differentiate the denominator and the numerator separately: $$\lim_{x\to\infty} \frac{\frac{d}{dx} e^x}{\frac{d}{dx} x^k}$$

title: Find the derivative
text: What is the answer of the function after L’Hôpital’s Rule is applied?

title: Rewrite the limit
text: After applying L’Hôpital’s Rule k times, the numerator is still $$e^x$$ and the denominator becomes the constant k! (k factorial).

subHints.title: Factorial Formula
subHints.text: Take a look at the denominator: each time we apply L’Hôpital’s Rule, the exponent of $$x$$ becomes a new factor and the power of $$x$$ decreases by $$1$$. After k applications, the denominator is k times $$(k-1)$$ times ... times $$1$$, which is k! (k factorial).

subHints.title: Explanation
subHints.text: No matter how many time we apply the L’Hôpital’s Rule, the limit will always have the form $$\frac{\infty}{\infty}$$. The derivative of $$e^x$$ on the numerator will always be the same. Meanwhile, as we apply the L’Hôpital’s Rule successively, the function in the denominator will behave: $$k x^{k-1}$$, $$k \left(k-1\right) x^{k-2}$$, k*(k-1)*(k-2)*x**(k-3),...,k!x,k!

title: Evaluate the limit
text: As $$x$$ approaches $$\infty$$, $$e^x$$ approaches infinity while k! is a constant, so the limit is $$\infty$$.
